answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 5 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the grove gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the dawn audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 42 variations of one paragraph as a result pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the vertex panel. That is 21 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
